transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Alex Moreno (Redwood CSM); Alyssa Park (Lantern Bio - Head of ML), Miguel Torres (Lantern Bio - Infra Lead), Samir Gupta (Lantern Bio - Product)

Summary:
Lantern Bio is evaluating Redwood for production inference of clinical summarization and downstream retrieval augmentation. Primary concerns are data residency, encryption/KMS, and predictable latency/cost. They are interested in a quickstart using free credits to validate time-to-first-token (TTFT) and run a few performance benchmarks before selecting Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Topics: quickstart credits, TTFT, hosted vs dedicated vs private, SOC2/KMS/HSM, VPC connectivity, pricing signals, POC scope and success criteria.

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Kim from Redwood, AE for your account. Quick intro round please?
[00:08] Alyssa: Hi I'm Alyssa, Head of ML at Lantern Bio. We own the models and evaluation.
[00:12] Miguel: Miguel, infra lead. I handle networking, VPCs, and compliance stuff.
[00:16] Samir: Samir, product. Running the summarization feature roadmap.
[00:19] Priya: Hi all, Priya Desai, solutions engineer. I'll do the deep techno bits.
[00:23] Jordan: Great. Agenda: quickstart and credits, expected TTFT, security requirements, then scope for a short pilot and next steps. Sound good?
[00:29] Alyssa: Yeah. We're mainly looking to prove out latency and cost for our summarization pipeline, also want to validate that we can keep patient PII on-prem or in our VPC.
[00:38] Priya: Totally. A lot of customers start on Hosted API with our free credits, we help them get to first token in under an hour — often minutes if you have the prompts ready. Then we measure token cost and latency profiles and advise on dedicated or private if isolation is required.
[00:49] Miguel: So quick question — when you say "hosted", are you storing any inputs? What's retention, and can we use our own KMS?
[00:56] Jordan: Good question. Hosted has configurable retention defaults; we have options for no persist, short-term logs, or customer-configured retention. For keys, we support customer-managed keys in our Private offering and we integrate with KMS for Dedicated in some cases. For Hosted we can do envelope encryption but for H S M style key control you likely want Private.
[01:14] Miguel: Got it. Any SOC2 or ISO docs we can share internally?
[01:18] Jordan: Yes — I'll attach our SOC 2 report and ISO summary in the follow up.
[01:22] Samir: On TTFT: our product managers are really sensitive to developer velocity. We need an estimate for how long devs spend from signup to a first successful inference with our sample prompt.
[01:31] Priya: Practically, with our SDK and quickstart notebook it's usually under 15 minutes for a developer to run a sample request. For a production-integrated flow — needing VPC, SSO, certs — that stretches to days depending on approvals. For the quick start with credits, we aim for minutes.
[01:47] Alyssa: Ok. For benchmarks we care about p95 latency for 256 token outputs and throughput for batch summarization jobs. Can you run a representative benchmark with our prompts?
[01:57] Priya: Yes. For that we typically do three runs: hosted baseline (our shared hosted infra), dedicated pool with reserved capacity, and a private VPC test if needed. We'll measure cold vs warm KV cache impact, batching, and quantization profiles. The benchmark spreadsheet will show tokens/sec and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:14] Miguel: You said KV cache — you mean K V cash? How does that work for long sequences?
[02:19] Priya: Sorry, K V cache — the key/value attention cache. It stores past activations to speed generation for incremental contexts. For long sequences we have cache eviction and prefix caching strategies. There's also continuous batching so many small requests can be coalesced at the runtime layer.
[02:33] Miguel: That sounds useful. For on-prem / VPC, how does egress work and do we need to open ports on our side?
[02:40] Alex: Typically for Private we run a control plane that can sit in the customer's VPC; data plane may stay within the VPC and we support peering options. We'll share our deployment doc but it does need a handful of outbound ports for telemetry and control, or a fully air-gapped on-prem package for regulated customers.
[02:58] Samir: When you talk about model selection, do you provide model variants and quantization recommendations?
[03:04] Priya: Yes, our Optimize recommendations give quantization profiles and variant suggestions depending on your latency and quality targets. During pilot we can try FP16 vs int8 quantized variants and measure hallucination/regression on your evaluation set.
[03:16] Alyssa: On hallucinations — we need to measure quality drift. Do you have eval tooling tied to prompts?
[03:21] Priya: We do. We can run your prompt set through nightly evals and hook alerts to regression thresholds. For the POC we'll set baselines and acceptance criteria like ROUGE/EM/SAM metrics you define.
[03:33] Miguel: Let's talk timeline. We want to have an answer on whether to go production by end of Q3. That means pilot in next two weeks ideally. Can Redwood support a 2-week trial with dedicated guidance?
[03:43] Jordan: Absolutely. Typical pilot is 2–4 weeks: free credits to validate TTFT and basic perf, plus a dedicated SE-led benchmark. If you need reserved latency we can propose Dedicated for the pilot with a temporary capacity reservation.
[03:56] Samir: Any rough cost signaling? We need to compare hosted payg vs reserved dedicated.
[04:02] Jordan: High level: Hosted is usage-based and great for prototyping. Dedicated gives predictable throughput for a monthly commit and better tail latency. Private has higher upfront but full control. I'll include a short pricing matrix in the follow up.
[04:14] Miguel: For Dedicated, can we bring our own model or do we need you'd host a curated artifact?
[04:20] Priya: You can bring your own model artifacts — we support standard model formats and will run an onboarding validation. If you bring a very large custom model, we coordinate kernel selection and quantization so it runs efficiently.
[04:32] Alyssa: That's important. We have a family of encoder-decoder models for summarization that are finetuned internally.
[04:38] Priya: Great, bring a representative snapshot and a small eval harness and we'll run compatibility checks.
[04:44] Miguel: Network and auth — do you support SAML/SSO and RBAC?
[04:48] Alex: Yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC, fine-grained roles, audit logs accessible via the Console or exported to customer logging endpoints. For Private we can integrate with on-prem identity providers.
[05:00] Samir: Any gotchas with data residency? We have EU patients and need the data to remain in EU for some flows.
[05:06] Jordan: We support region pinning and private deployments that ensure data plane stays in specified region or on-prem. We'll note that in the follow up and map out options.
[05:14] Alyssa: For the quickstart — what do we need from our side to get to first token?
[05:18] Priya: Minimal: a Redwood account, API key (we'll provision trial credits), and a sample prompt set. If you want to test in your VPC we also need your network contact details so we can schedule the VPC bits.
[05:28] Miguel: Who on our side will be involved in the pilot setup? I'll be the infra owner and Alyssa will provide the model and prompts, Samir will define product acceptance metrics.
[05:36] Jordan: Perfect. We'll propose a schedule: Day 0 - account + credits, Day 1 - run sample notebook, Day 2-5 - initial benchmarks, Week 2 - review and decision.
[05:46] Alyssa: Sounds reasonable. Can you commit to a benchmark that includes p95 latency for 256 token outputs and cost per 1k tokens?
[05:53] Priya: Yes that's part of our standard bench. We'll also include warm/cold cache runs and a dedicated worker run if you want low tail latency numbers.
[06:02] Miguel: Security detail question: are logs encrypted at rest with customer keys for Hosted?
[06:06] Jordan: Hosted by default uses our managed keys, but we can enable encrypt-at-rest with CMKs for certain accounts, or you can choose Private for full key ownership. I'll note that in the follow up doc.
[06:16] Samir: For the pilot acceptance criteria — we want less than X latency and cost under Y. We still need to pick X and Y.
[06:22] Alyssa: For now set p95 below 800ms for a 256 token generation, cost target TBD — we'll share the target.
[06:29] Miguel: 800ms p95 is doable in dedicated; hosted may vary.
[06:33] Priya: We'll validate both.
[06:35] Jordan: Ok quick clarifying — any blockers around legal or procurement?
[06:39] Samir: We'll need a standard NDA and an SOW for the pilot. Procurement will review SOC2 and data processing addendum.
[06:46] Jordan: We'll attach the NDA and DPA in the follow up.
[06:49] Alex: Also want to call out that for some customers we run a short smoke test that includes sample PII redaction to ensure no data retention concerns.
[06:58] Alyssa: Good. We'll provide a redacted sample set and a small script to simulate our production traffic.
[07:04] Priya: That will be perfect. For the benchmarking we also ask for a target QPS and concurrency profile.
[07:10] Miguel: We'll provide typical concurrency: 6 workers at peak, batching up to 16.
[07:15] Priya: Noted.
[07:17] Jordan: Any other questions before we capture next steps?
[07:20] Samir: One more — how easy is it to switch from Hosted to Dedicated later?
[07:24] Priya: It's designed to be seamless from an API standpoint. You can pin model versions and rollout policies. The main work is capacity planning and possibly VPC setup for Private.
[07:33] Alyssa: Are there tooling differences?
[07:35] Priya: Same Console features mostly, Dedicated exposes reserved metrics and capacity controls.
[07:40] Jordan: Ok let's recap and assign actions. Jordan will send SOC2, pricing matrix, and SOW. Priya will share the quickstart notebook + SDK examples and benchmark template. Miguel will provide sample prompts and concurrency targets.
[07:53] Miguel: I'll get that to you by next week.
[07:56] Jordan: Great. Follow ups: schedule the benchmark deep dive for week of 2026-07-20.
[08:02] Alex: I'll spin up the meeting invite and include an attendee list.
[08:05] Alyssa: Thank you.
[08:07] Jordan: Thanks all.

[08:10] (call ends)
